text:
Anna: hey team — flagging a small design follow-up: can we make the smoke sampler hardware-aware?
Kevin: curious, what do you mean by hardware-aware?
Anna: like: pick golden samples differently for A100 vs T4 pools so the bench exercise exercises realistic seqlen / kv-cache patterns per class.
Maria: +1. Right now the sampler is uniform across models and that skews perf numbers when we compare quantized vs fp16 runs.
Sam: agree. tradeoffs? more complexity in the pipeline, and we need to store multiple golden sets per model variant.
Anna: tradeoffs yes. proposal: keep a small stratified set per hardware class (a, b, c) keyed by observed seqlen distribution in telemetry. cheap to store (hundreds of inputs) but better signal.
Kevin: how do we map a model to hardware class? annotation in the model manifest? or infer from runtime preference?
Maria: manifest + runtime override seems best. manifest has a "preferred_hardware" field already in the registry, we can extend it to a list.
Sam: also need sampling logic: for long-tail seqlens we should upweight samples that touch KV cache. Maybe weight by P(seqlen>512) from recent traffic.
Anna: exactly. rough pseudocode:
```
weights = mix(global_seqlen_hist[hw_class], model_seqlen_hist, fallback=uniform)
sample = weighted_choice(candidates, weights)
```
Kevin: ok. storage: keep per-model candidate pool + per-hw-class seed lists. When we onboard new hardware, we generate seeds via telemetry job.
Maria: latency/cost impact: more bench variants -> multiply bench time. We should gate this behind a quick-smoke budget. e.g., run hardware-aware smoke only for Dedicated/D/VPC targets or when model traffic > X qps.
Sam: yep. fallback path: if no hw-specific seeds, use global seeds and mark the run as "cross-hw-proxy" in the report. that helps downstream metric comparison.
Anna: I also want a small CLI to snapshot hw seeds for a model: `rbx onboard snapshot-seeds --hw a100 --size 200`. That lets solutions/SE reproduce locally.
Kevin: can OnboardBot surface mismatches? e.g., if model manifest prefers a100 but onboarding bench runs on t4, post a warning.
OnboardBot: WARNING: model pref `preferred_hardware: [a100]` != bench_host_hw: t4. Recommended: rerun hardware-aware-smoke or add `accept_t4_fallback: true` to manifest.
Maria: nice. one more: evals/quality comparisons must normalize for hardware — we should add `bench_hardware` tag to eval artifacts and to rollout decisions.
Sam: implementation tasks: 1) schema change in registry (manifest list), 2) sampling service change, 3) small storage table for hw seeds, 4) OnboardBot warning. I can pick 2+3.
Anna: I'll own the manifest schema and CLI. Kevin can wire the OnboardBot bits? @Kevin
Kevin: sure, will add the warning and a short runbook for reruns.
Maria: timeline? this seems low-risk, 2 sprint feature if no infra surprises.
Anna: putting a rough plan in the RFC follow-up doc. Quick question: do we want to version the seeds so runs are reproducible?
Sam: yes — store seed-set id + hw class in bench metadata. add that id to bench artifacts.
Anna: sweet. thanks all. next step: I'll create a tiny RFC PR outlining schema + sampling algo and ping reviewers.
Kevin: 👍
Maria: :thumbsup:
Sam: :rocket:
